dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: My fellow disciple and I trained in the martial arts from childhood. Our quest was to fight the forces of evil and protect all that is sacred in this world. But this was no easy task without the aid of a <color=#00E1FFFF>Vision</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: We two sought refuge here to train ourselves further and to seek the <color=#00E1FFFF>Visions</color> that we desired. We erected this monument in testament to our endeavors.

dialogues.text: Touch the monument

dialogues.text: Touch the monument

dialogues.text: Leave for Now

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: I was fortunate enough to receive my <color=#00E1FFFF>Vision</color>. But still, there was doubt in my mind: Is it truly within the power of mere mortals to one day cleanse the world of the monsters that have long plagued it? And how different from mankind are these monsters to begin with, save in outward appearance? Is it not so that just like us, they, too, speak; they, too, build; and they, too, feel love and hate, joy and grief...

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: I hereby inscribe my mind's greatest perplexion onto this monument. O, reader in the far-flung future, will you be the one to resolve this riddle?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: We who would protect our way of life, are we but making blind judgments on good and evil based on what our small minds can conceive?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Monsters wreak havoc all across this world, and we who seek to protect it would do well to remember: Monsters deserve nothing more than the merciless slaughter they will get!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Touch the monument

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: These preceding questions three, I approached my fellow disciple and asked them of he. But he chastised me, accusing me of abandoning my duty, and marched off furiously. May the true answers to these three questions bring peace to the world. In my time, I have sought the wisdom of ancient texts from all corners of the world, I have hidden myself here in quiet meditation, and I have studied the language of monsters; all this I have done in the hope of understanding their true nature. I erect this monument to be my witness when the one comes who can resolve these questions once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Touch the monument

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Are monsters truly evil by nature?

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Are mortals and adepti truly good by nature?

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Future reader, I know not whether you bear the answers to my questions.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Anyone who reads these words must surely be of the same nature as I.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>If it is of interest to you, I have buried what few treasures I own by the pool. Retrieve them with my blessing.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: But please never forget these questions three. I pray that there will come a day when you are equipped to answer them.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>Visions</color>... They truly hail from a realm beyond. People say that they are a gift from the divine, but none can say who will receive one and why.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Ancient texts hold that the divine looks down with compassion on the mortal realm, and bestows <color=#00E1FFFF>Visions</color> upon the worthy to help them fight against evil and protect the world. But I... I no longer burn with a desire to banish monsters. I just want to communicate with them. To understand them.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: This <color=#00E1FFFF>Vision</color>... It is of no use to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: To the one who views this monument: Seek ye first the monuments in the mountain, and only then return to the one erected here.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Treasure
dialogues.text: Any who earnestly seeks to resolve my perplexion should seek first the monuments in the mountain, and view them in order.
